title: Windscreen wipers
prompt: A labelled bench teaching model of the page 49 wipers sweeps a small glass panel. Wet uses an external dropper to place droplets on the glass. Wipe powers the motor worm reduction, crank and connecting rod, reciprocating the rack so its blade-shaft pinions rock the wipers. Stop removes the motor drive at its current phase. See-through exposes the worm, driven wheel, eccentric crank pin, connecting rod, guided rack, pinions and blade pivots. The dropper is a specimen fixture. Do not add a washer pump or claim automatic parking.
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation shows a crank-driven rack rocking two wipers across wet glass.
adaptation: Rack-and-pinion teaching model with external dropper gantry, illustrative scale and slowed motion. No washer plumbing or automatic parking.
truthNotes: Single crank phase determines the fixed-length rod, guided rack and both blade shafts.
Worm, driven wheel and rack teeth are simplified tooth forms, not manufacturing geometry.
The external dropper and its gantry are teaching fixtures, excluded from anatomy. Drops adhere to glass until crossed by a rubber edge. Runoff, inertia and friction are omitted.
Stop freezes the current phase and does not return blades to a park position.

telemetry.reason: Standalone static figure. No production telemetry is installed. Live verification untested.
